newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian test run for new euro set for the autumn.
newsitem.headline: Italian test run for new euro set for the autumn.

text.p: Italians will get their first chance to shop with Europe's planned single currency for two months this autumn in rural Tuscany, Treasury under-secretary Roberto Pinza said on Tuesday.
Starting in October, retailers, restaurants and banks in Fiesole and Pontassieve, two small towns near the central Italian city of Florence, will do business in euros, Pinza told a news conference.
Consumers will be able to exchange the Italian currency at local banks at a rate of 2,000 lire ($1.18) per euro, he added.
The test trial coins will be almost exact reproductions of the euro, with slight differences that will render them void once the real European currency is launched, Pinza said.

If European economic and monetary union (EMU) moves forward as planned, citizens in participating countries will see their national currency phased out between January and July 2002 and replaced with the euro.
Similar trial programmes, sponsored jointly by the European Commission and by national governments, have been held in Germany and France.
In Italy, the initiative is part of an information campaign for the euro that includes the free distribution of explanatory pamphlets at news-stands and by mail, Pinza said.
Italy is one of the most enthusiastic supporters of planned EMU and has swallowed huge amounts of harsh budget medicine in recent years in a bid to meet tough criteria for euro aspirants.
Euro founder members are due to be chosen at a special European Union summit next May.
